view_record.note: Five genuinely new open diacritic loci received one crop each. The first apparaît used an existing crop. The low point-pair was inspected within the already-created first-connaît crop; no additional crop was made.

changes.place: Opening assertion, first apparaît, after Π₁(X,I)
changes.scan_shows: The mark above i is a compact upright oval point. It has no apex and two arms. The same reused crop also contains a clearly angular mathematical hat below/right, which is a graphic comparison rather than a rule for prose accents.

changes.place: Second apparaît, after et où Π₁(C,I)
changes.scan_shows: A single compact dark point stands over i. Its outline is slightly triangular but does not show two separate sloping arms or an extended accent. Read plain i at this occurrence.

changes.place: Middle clause, sous-groupoïde before the inserted plein
changes.scan_shows: One round detached point is visible over i in this word. The later divided groupoï-/de has two separately spaced points, as the existing groupoid_phrase crop shows. The local single-point spelling is therefore retained here without a supplied diaeresis.

changes.place: First connaît, in est connue quand on connaît l’opération
changes.scan_shows: The detached i mark is one short thick oblique stroke. It favors a dot-like point but could compress an accent; no distinct pair of circumflex arms can be separated. Keep plain i first and the circumflex alternative.

changes.place: Second connaît, after the full stop: Si on connaît l’action
changes.scan_shows: The detached i mark is a compact rounded point, rather than the oblique stroke in the earlier occurrence. No circumflex shape is visible. Read literal connait.

changes.place: Two small points immediately below/right of the final t in the first connaît
changes.scan_shows: Two small detached dark points are visible at the right edge of the first connaît, well below its rising word baseline and to the left of the following l’opération. The upper mark is angular/comma-like and the lower one rounded. They lie in the gap above the next line containing Π̂₁(C,Ĩ), roughly 80 pixels above that line’s highest tilde/hat marks; they do not attach to that following formula. Their presence as ink is clear, but their unusually low position leaves punctuation versus incidental pen-points unresolved. The proposed \unsure{:} records a possible colon only.

existing_apparatus_review.outcome: All nine inherited substantive readings are supported. The new proposals concern agreed witness diacritics and a newly noticed pair of low points.
specific_confirmations: qui lui est has no même.
du groupoï- / de is singular, with de completing the split noun.
The closing upper words and separately crossed upper formula have distinct deletion states.

notation_findings.finding: All thirteen live group signs and the cancelled closing group sign were inspected. Capitals have a flat cap and two legs; hats remain where written. The middle target after du groupoïde is unhatted.
Prime, tilde and zero remain distinct. Saturation I-prime and the later I-prime are supported; the C-group in the lower paragraph has a wavy tilde over I.
The two contextually surprising middle U forms are plainly U and remain so. No curve letter C has been supplied from mathematical expectation.
Both acting-group signs are plain single-stem capital Gamma; no outlined font is introduced.

hand_log_additions.scope: Two apparait forms and the second connait have compact points; the first connait has a short oblique mark and retains doubt.
hand_log_additions.evidence: Each occurrence was inspected independently; no page-wide normalization was applied.

hand_log_additions.evidence: The new audit_meme crop shows a conspicuous raised return joined to the first e. The inherited même is retained; absence of a detached caret does not alone imply plain e.

notes: Complete second reading of this page only, against C, H and consolidated text. The original image and each existing native half were viewed once; no OCR, external research, new halves or compilation.
All nine supplied inventory elements are present. The possible low colon is additionally inventoried because the two points are physical ink, although their function remains unresolved.
The four inherited uncertainties remain explicit: cancelled X, concretement/grave, cancelled La, upper action/opération. Existing resolved f and cancelled on remain supported.
Both C and H spell both occurrences apparaît, both occurrences connaît, and sous-groupoïde. Their exact local spellings are recorded for every proposed diacritic change.

Final lui-même was genuinely open at native size; its one close crop supports the connected raised ê gesture, so no change is proposed. A secure ê is also visible in the full revêtement from the native top half. Mathematical hats provide further graphic comparisons but are not used as a universal prose-accent rule.

Punctuation proposal A088-06 is deliberately low-confidence. If the main reader judges the point-pair incidental rather than punctuation, keep the physical trace in inventory/notes and do not manufacture a certain colon.
The covering and quotient assertions were read for notation and context, but no proof or computation was undertaken. No mathematical check event is claimed.
The point-pair is a separate proposed locus from the first connai-t diacritic. Presence as punctuation and the colon interpretation are both uncertain; the pair is not described as a definite colon.
